support.locus: Fled Bricrenn, Windisch Irische Texte I (same horse catalogue, second copy, and Windisch's glossary entry less-lethan 'mit breiten Hanken')

words.lemma: clun (fem. noun 'hip, thigh', lenited after dwy 'two')

cognate: Welsh clun = Av. sraoni- = Skt śroṇi- (*ḱlowni-, also Lat. clūnis); Welsh llydan / OIr. lethan = Av. pərəθu-, Skt pṛthu- (root *pleth₂- 'broad'). The adjective is a different formation in Celtic (*-ano- vs *-u-), but the root is the same.
drift_or_renewal: Indo-Iranian keeps the compound (Av. pərəθu.sraoni-, Skt pṛthuśroṇī); Welsh breaks it up into a predicative phrase ('her two hips were broad'), with the *-ano- adjective. In Irish the head noun is replaced by less 'haunch', and the 'broad' adjective goes second as a descriptive compound.
shared_syntax: body-part noun + 'broad' (*pleth₂-), one item in a list of bodily-dimension descriptors: Av. dərəzi.yaoxəδra-, bərəzi.pāδa-, pərəθu.vara-, pərəθu.sraoni-; Welsh dwy glun ... llydan, ... traet a glinyeu ... bras; OIr. ech líath lesslethan ... uchtlethan, baslethan uchtlethan ... druimlethan
context: Formal head-to-foot description (portrait catalogue) of a mighty or marvellous being. The Avestan list is of epithets of the warrior Vayu (Vayu Yašt, Yt 15; corpus id YtWay12.13f), and Mithra's horses are pərəθu.safa- 'broad-hoofed' (Yt 10). The Welsh is the hideous maiden's portrait at Arthur's court in Peredur. The Irish lists are the portraits of Cú Chulainn's horses in Fled Bricrenn. Epic Sanskrit pṛthuśroṇī is a stock epithet of beautiful women. Against the parallel: the Welsh portrait is grotesque, Sanskrit uses the word for beauty, and Avestan uses it for divine might. 'Broad hips/chest' is also a natural descriptive collocation, so chance is a real possibility. What the parallel rests on is the exact Celtic/Indo-Iranian match of both lexemes (*ḱlowni- + *pleth₂-) inside a body-catalogue. Peredur is a late (13th-c.) prose romance.
phrase: *pl̥th₂u-ḱlowni- 'broad-hipped' (Av. pərəθu.sraoni-, Skt pṛthuśroṇī-; MW y dwy glun ... yn llydan)

note: One low claim: broad-hipped *pl̥th₂u- + *ḱlowni- in body catalogues (MW clun llydan ~ Av. pərəθu.sraoni-, Skt pṛthuśroṇī; OIr. -lethan horse portraits as context). Considered and left out: OIr. ech líath ~ ON fölvan jó (BS-4b47a), since a grey/pale horse is generic description; also MW rhif sêr 'number of stars' (biblical, no cognate partner). The other bundles are automatic root co-occurrence with no shared wording.
